item.title: Alderman Rodney Jele granted bail pending extortion trial
item.description: Danisa Masuku, Court Reporter FORMER Bulawayo city councillor, Alderman Rodney Jele, who was previously denied bail by the lower court, has been granted bail by the High Court pending trial. Jele was legally represented by Mr Kholwane Ngwenya of TJ Mabhikwa and Partners during a successful appeal heard on Tuesday before Bulawayo High Court Judge, Justice Bongani Ndlovu. In his ruling, Justice Ndlovu upheld the appeal, stating: “The decision of Provincial Magistrate Mr Isheunesu Mathoba to refuse him bail is hereby set aside and substituted with an order admitting the appellant to bail pending trial on a charge of extortion.” Jele’s co-accused—Deputy Mayor Edwin Ndlovu, Councillor Mxolisi Mahlangu, Councillor Ashton Mhlanga, and Councillor Ntandoyenkosi Ndlovu—were also granted bail pending trial subject to stringent conditions. The four serving councillors were ordered to surrender their passports, reside at their given residential addresses, and report to designated police stations in Bulawayo three times a week until the criminal matter is finalised. Both Jele and his co-accused are expected back in court on 24 September 2026. The criminal allegations stem from a 50-year commercial lease agreement granted by the Bulawayo City Council to Mkhuze Global Investments in March 2023 for the development of a local hotel. The State alleges that the four serving councillors, acting in cahoots with former councillor Jele, later demanded a payout of US$52 000 from the local businessman in connection with the lease. State prosecutor Mr Pedzisai told the court that the accused persons approached the businessman in August this year and informed him that rival businesspeople were heavily interested in the commercial stand. “In August this year, the accused persons approached the businessman and told him that other businesspeople were interested in the stand and were prepared to pay US$52 000 to have his lease cancelled,” said Mr Pedzisai. The businessman was told that he had to match the US$52 000 payment if he wished to retain his hotel lease. He subsequently approached the Zimbabwe Anti-Corruption Commission (ZACC), which launched an undercover sting operation. The anti-graft operation culminated in Jele’s arrest after the complainant handed over the demanded US$52 000. Jele was caught red-handed while counting the money at the complainant’s house. Following his initial arrest, his lower court application for bail was dismissed by the provincial magistrate, forcing him to remain in custody until the successful High Court appeal. (via The Sunday News) #Zimbabwe #ZimbabweNews

item.title: Confederation of Zimbabwe Retailers appoints new national chairman
item.description: Sikhulekelani Moyo THE Confederation of Zimbabwe Retailers (CZR) has appointed Cde Moses Chihuri as its new national chairman for a two-year tenure. In a statement, the CZR president, board, executive and management congratulated Cde Chihuri on his appointment and expressed confidence in his leadership. “The Confederation of Zimbabwe Retailers president, board, executive and management wishes to extend its heartfelt congratulations to Cde Moses Chihuri on his appointment as national chairman of the Confederation of Zimbabwe Retailers for a two-year tenure,” read the statement. The retail body said it looked forward to Cde Chihuri’s contribution towards advancing the interests of the sector. “We wish you success and strength as you assume this important responsibility. We look forward to your leadership, commitment and contribution towards advancing the interests of the retail and wholesale sector,” said CZR. The Confederation of Zimbabwe Retailers is the apex body representing the retail and wholesale sector in Zimbabwe and advocates for a conducive business environment, formalisation of trade and consumer protection. (via The Sunday News) #Zimbabwe #ZimbabweNews

item.title: NSSA moves to extend social security to informal workers
item.description: Theseus Mauruki Shambare in VICTORIA FALLS THE National Social Security Authority (NSSA) is on the verge of piloting a new social security scheme targeting workers in Zimbabwe’s informal economy, as the Tripartite Negotiating Forum (TNF) Global Summit enters its second day in Victoria Falls. The proposed scheme is part of wider discussions at the summit on employment creation, social protection and building an inclusive global economy capable of responding to changing labour-market realities. NSSA Director of Social Security and Benefits, Actuarial and Schemes Development, Mr Shepherd Muperi, said the authority had undertaken extensive research to develop a social security programme suited to the circumstances of informal economy workers. The initiative is being developed with the International Labour Organisation (ILO), with stakeholder consultations having been conducted to determine the priorities of informal workers and ensure that the scheme is affordable and sustainable. “As we speak, we are at the verge of almost implementing or piloting a specific, appropriate and suitable social security scheme for workers in the informal economy,” Mr Muperi said. The proposed expansion comes against a backdrop of a labour market in which a significant proportion of workers operate outside conventional formal employment arrangements, limiting their access to social protection schemes traditionally based on employer-employee relationships. Mr Muperi said existing schemes had largely been designed around formal employment, stable salaries and identifiable employers, making them less suited to informal workers and emerging forms of employment such as platform work. “We appreciate that they may not be able to join the formal schemes that we have that are based on employer-employee relationships, because, traditionally, these social security schemes were designed for employment-based where there is employer and employee and stable salaries,” he said. The proposed scheme will seek to incorporate incentives that respond to the practical challenges facing informal businesses and workers. Mr Muperi said these could include access to decent workspaces and affordable funding to help informal businesses develop and grow. “The challenge is that people want informal economy workers to contribute even towards taxes, but the focus should be more on: how are we supporting them to develop their business, to grow them?” he said. He said informal workers had also been involved in the design process, helping NSSA identify the social risks and benefits they considered priorities. “The design is coming from with them, and they have expressed their priority needs in terms of all the life risks to say: this is what we want covered,” Mr Muperi said. The issue of extending social protection to workers outside the formal economy also featured prominently in the summit’s discussions on the future of decent work. Director of the ILO Country Office for Zimbabwe and Namibia, Ms Philile Ntombikayise Masuku, said Zimbabwe should move towards implementing its recently endorsed formalisation strategy while progressively extending social protection to informal and platform workers. “We need to commit to making sure that it is implemented and also commit to the gradual extension of social protection to informal workers and also the workers in the platform economy,” she said. Mr Muperi said social security could also play a role in mobilising domestic resources for national development, with pooled funds potentially supporting infrastructure and productive investments. He cited dams, roads, energy projects and industry as areas where social security funds could contribute to development while supporting economic activity and employment creation. “Social security is acknowledged worldwide as a very important vehicle for mobilizing local resources for national development,” he said. As the TNF Global Summit continues, the proposed NSSA scheme adds a practical dimension to the broader call for social protection to reach workers across Zimbabwe’s changing labour market, including those outside traditional formal employment. (via The Sunday News) #Zimbabwe #ZimbabweNews
